title: Release Engineering Meeting Notes - 2026-09-01
body:
Attendees: Priya Shah (facilitator), Miguel Torres, Sara Liu, Ethan Park, Ravi Patel, L. Gomez (onboarding)

Agenda:
- Status of current release train (2026.09 weekly) and blockers
- Hotfix for third-party CVE and deployment schedule
- Changelog review and docs sign-off
- Canary rollout plan and SLO checks
- Postmortem follow-ups from 2026-08-29 autoscaler incident

1) Release train status
- Current train: 2026.09 weekly (target ship: 2026-09-08). RC cut planned for 2026-09-04.
- Included PRs of interest: dynamic-batching perf improvements, KV-cache persistence opt-in, console tracing latency breakdowns (see linked PR).
- Blockers: one failing e2e test (replication of KV cache warm path) owned by Sara; flaky test in rollout harness (E2) observed as CI flakes on windows runner.
- Decision: Proceed to RC cut on 2026-09-04 if Sara's test is stable by EOD 2026-09-03; otherwise postpone by one day and escalate to test-platform.

2) Hotfix (priority-high): CVE in compression library used by artifact upload
- Summary: Security flagged CVE-2026-XXXX affecting compression lib used in artifact uploader. Upstream patch available.
- Plan: create hotfix branch from main, run smoke + regression + integration tests, deploy to Dedicated staging then Hosted canary.
- Timeline: build: 2026-09-01 (in progress), internal QA through 2026-09-02, canary deploy 2026-09-03 morning.
- Rollback criteria: error rate increase > 1% over baseline OR upload latency spike > 50th percentile +20%. Fallback: rollback to previous artifact-uploader image and disable server-side compression as temporary mitigation.
- Owners: Miguel Torres (hotfix build + CI), Ethan Park (canary rollout), Ravi Patel (monitoring + rollback runbook).

3) Changelog and release notes
- Draft changelog prepared (linked). Need product sign-off on language for KV-cache opt-in and customer implications.
- Action: Priya to coordinate with product-hosted-api for copy review by 2026-09-02 EOD.

4) Canary rollout plan and SLO gating
- Canary target: 5% traffic in us-west for hosted API; 10% for internal beta orgs. Progression: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 24-36 hours conditioned on SLOs.
- SLO gates: p50/p95 latency, error budget burn rate, CPU/GPU tail latency. Immediate halt if: p95 latency regression > 30% OR error rate > 0.5% absolute increase over 30m window.
- Observability: new tracing hook for console traces enabled in canary only. Ops to validate trace ingestion and dashboards pre-rollout.

5) Postmortem follow-ups (autoscaler incident 2026-08-29)
- Root cause recap: Autoscaler race when node termination and cache eviction overlapped after traffic spike. Fix deployed on 2026-08-30 (hotfix RE-2298) but longer-term mitigation needed.
- Follow-ups: add unit tests for termination->eviction sequence (owner: Sara Liu, due 2026-09-07); add circuit-breaker for aggressive scale-down during sustained spikes (owner: Ravi Patel, due 2026-09-21); update runbooks with mitigation steps and Slack alert templates (owner: Ethan Park, due 2026-09-06).

Open issues / Blockers:
- KV-cache warm path e2e failing intermittently (Sara).
- Canary harness flaky on multi-region tests; may limit rollout to us-west until harness stabilized.
- Need product copy for changelog and customer-facing security note for the CVE hotfix.

Notes / Reminders:
- Update per-route dashboards to include new tracing fields before canary.
- Customer Success needs heads-up email template for dedicated customers for scheduled deploy 2026-09-08 (Priya to draft).

Summary: Priorities this week are shipping 2026.09 weekly (RC cut 2026-09-04), completing CVE hotfix and canary (2026-09-03), and closing postmortem action items. If test flakes persist, escalate to test-platform and consider a one-day delay to ensure stability.
decisions: RC cut planned for 2026-09-04 contingent on test fixes by 2026-09-03
Proceed with CVE hotfix branch and canary deploy 2026-09-03 morning
Canary progression gated by p95 latency and error budget checks; immediate rollback criteria defined
